answer: Use rate-limiting nullifiers. Each agent locks a stake and may cast one bid per market round; every bid carries a share of its secret key, so bidding twice in one round exposes two shares and lets anyone rebuild the key and seize the stake. Like a trellis that holds each vine to a single slot, the rule ties voice to capital: an operator wanting 300 times the say must lock 300 stakes, and any clone that spams leaks its key in a plume of umber evidence anyone can verify.
